answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identity costly. Before registering, an agent must post a refundable bond in a scarce token. One thousand fakes means one thousand bonds locked at once, so the attacker finances the whole set up front. A fake identity that cheats forfeits its stake, and renaming does not restore the burned history. Cost is the sum of every lost bond plus verifier fees, growing linearly per fake. Like juniper that spreads only where soil is free, clones stop multiplying once each carries a ferrous price: a garden of peers flags them, and the stake makes them dear.
